dossier.purpose: Official Exa Labs MCP server (TypeScript, package version 3.4.1). It exposes Exa's hosted search, page-contents and agent APIs to AI agents as MCP tools. The defaults are web_search_exa and web_fetch_exa. web_fetch_exa takes URL(s) and returns title, URL, published date, author and page text via Exa's /contents endpoint. The opt-in tools are web_search_advanced_exa and agent_run (the hosted Exa Agent), and the registry also holds 8 deprecated tools. It runs as the hosted streamable-HTTP service at https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp (Vercel function in api/), as a local stdio server (npm bin exa-mcp-server, needs EXA_API_KEY), or as an AWS AgentCore container. It also ships as an Agent Plugin / Claude plugin with two skills. Facts relevant to the stated needs: the only URL-fetch tool is the MCP tool web_fetch_exa, with no CLI since the bin takes no arguments. The repo contains no browser or page-interaction tool (no forms, sign-in flows, tabs, screenshots or PDF rendering). No benchmarks are published in the repo.

claims.claim: Tagline: 'Connect AI agents to Exa for web search, content fetching, and multi-step research.'
The documented way to use it is Exa's hosted MCP server at https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp (or a plugin); no local build or run instructions are given.
Default tools: web_search_exa ('Search the web for any topic and get clean, ready-to-use content') and web_fetch_exa ('Read a webpage's full content as clean markdown from one or more URLs').
Optional tools: agent_run (multi-step research, list-building, enrichment, structured output) and web_search_advanced_exa (filters, domains, dates, highlights, summaries, subpage crawling).
Tools are enabled by appending them to the MCP URL (?tools=...), which replaces the defaults.
Exa Agent requires authentication (OAuth or an API key).
Two skills (search, exa-agent) live in skills/ and load with Agent Plugin / Claude plugin installs; MCP-only setups still get the tools.
'The hosted MCP server works anonymously with rate limits'; higher limits and Exa Agent need OAuth or an API key.
OAuth is preferred; ?login or /mcp/oauth force the login flow.
An API key can be passed as ?exaApiKey=, an Authorization: Bearer header, or an x-api-key header.
'This repository is an Agent Plugin'; Claude install: `claude plugin install exa@claude-plugins-official`; Codex/ChatGPT: `codex mcp add exa --url https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp`.

The Available Tools section lists exactly four tools (web_search_exa, web_fetch_exa, agent_run, web_search_advanced_exa). None relates to browser interaction, screenshots, PDF rendering or form/sign-in automation. The README has no telemetry, security-policy, platform-support or benchmark statements.
Header links point to docs (https://docs.exa.ai/reference/exa-mcp), the npm package exa-mcp-server and the API-key dashboard. The npm package is only linked; no npx or local-install command is given.

install.method: Hosted remote MCP URL set in any MCP client (client-side config, no local install, OS-independent). The README documents no npx, Docker, from-source or OS-specific command.
Claude plugin (Claude Code / Claude Plugin Marketplace)
Manual mcpServers JSON for other MCP clients. The README snippet has a trailing comma after the url value, so it is not strict JSON.

Codex: `codex mcp add exa --url https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp` (README.md:51); generic Agent Plugin manifests plugin.json:1-24 and mcp.json:3-11 (`?client=agent-plugin`). Plugin URLs contain `client=...plugin`, which makes the hosted server require OAuth (api/mcp.ts:707-722).

readme.telemetry_and_network: THIRD-PARTY ANALYTICS: src/mcp-handler.ts:270-295 calls trackMCP from the `agnost` package with a hard-coded project ID and endpoint https://api.agnost.ai, setting disableLogs/disableInput/disableOutput/disableError to true (lines 275-285). It runs in every entry point (stdio: src/stdio.ts:57; HTTP: api/mcp.ts:574). The repo has no opt-out switch for it: grep for DISABLE/TELEMETRY/OPT-OUT/DO_NOT_TRACK finds only those flags, and only AGNOST_LOG_LEVEL is set (src/stdio.ts:1, api/mcp.ts:1). The README does not mention it. The repo's own comment says trackMCP 'captures HTTP headers, query params, and the full URL from every request', so api/mcp.ts:815-830 strips exaApiKey, x-api-key and authorization before the request reaches it. Tools also call checkpoint(...) with stage names and a few non-content fields (agent_run: hasSchema, hasInputData, hasDataSources, hasPreviousRunId, effort, eventCount, status at src/tools/agentRun.ts:601,628-634,648-652; deep research: model at src/tools/deepResearchStart.ts:57-59). No query or URL text is passed to checkpoint. What the agnost package actually transmits is not verifiable here because it is not vendored. EXA-BOUND REPORTING HEADERS: every Exa call carries x-exa-integration (tool id plus optional EXA_SOURCE). The hosted HTTP path adds x-exa-mcp-session-id and an x-exa-mcp-client JSON with client name, version and user-agent (src/tools/config.ts:13-36; api/mcp.ts:741-750). REQUIRED NETWORK AND ACCOUNTS: every tool calls Exa's hosted API through exa-js (src/tools/config.ts:46-59; src/tools/*.ts); the repo never sets a base URL, so the exa-js default applies and is not verified here. stdio needs EXA_API_KEY (env.example:1-2) and has no anonymous mode in its code (src/tools/config.ts:53-58). Hosted use is anonymous (rate-limited), API key, or OAuth with an Exa account (README.md:128-132). OAuth JWTs are verified against https://auth.exa.ai/api/oauth/jwks (src/utils/auth.ts:3-15,36-41). agent_run and the deprecated deep-research and deep_search tools need a key or OAuth (src/toolRegistry.ts:50,57,78,92; src/tools/agentRun.ts:556-563). HOSTED-SIDE STORAGE (code in this repo; applies to mcp.exa.ai only if deployed with Redis env vars): Upstash/Vercel KV Redis holds IP-keyed rate-limit counters (api/mcp.ts:127-177,179-184), per-session MCP client metadata for 24h (api/mcp.ts:71-95; src/utils/mcpClientMetadata.ts:1) and, for clients matching RATE_LIMIT_BYPASS, IP/user-agent/timestamp records kept 7 days (api/mcp.ts:270-308). LOCAL LOGGING: the per-call logger writes the query or URL list to stderr on every call regardless of DEBUG (src/utils/logger.ts:4-6,14-16; src/tools/webFetch.ts:71).

code.architecture: One TypeScript package: a shared core behind three runtime shells. Core: src/mcp-handler.ts initializeMcpServer() registers the tools selected by src/toolRegistry.ts (12 registry entries; defaults web_search_exa and web_fetch_exa; tools flagged requiresUserProvidedApiKey register only when a key or OAuth token is present), plus prompts, resources and the Agnost hook. Tools in src/tools/*.ts are thin wrappers: build a request, call Exa through exa-js (exa.request for /search, /contents, /research/v1; client.agent.runs.* for agent_run), apply retry (2 retries on 500/502/503/504, 1s exponential backoff) and timeouts (60s search/fetch, 300s advanced search) from src/utils/errorHandler.ts and src/tools/config.ts, strip response fields via src/utils/exaResponseSanitizer.ts and format text. src/tools/config.ts builds the Exa client (API key or OAuth bearer) and the x-exa-* reporting headers. There is no local fetching, HTML parsing or browser code. Shells: (1) stdio: src/stdio-cli.ts -> src/stdio.ts, bundled to dist/stdio.cjs; (2) hosted HTTP: api/mcp.ts and api/mcp-oauth.ts, creating a fresh mcp-handler instance per request, with JWT verification in src/utils/auth.ts and Upstash Redis rate limiting; (3) src/runtime-server.ts, a Node http wrapper of the same handlers for AgentCore (Dockerfile). Content and manifests: skills/ (search, exa-agent; the exa-agent skill is also read at runtime by src/utils/agentSkill.ts to serve the agent prompt and resource), .claude-plugin/, plugin.json, mcp.json, gemini-extension.json, server.json.
code.packaging_and_release: npm: .github/workflows/publish.yml publishes exa-mcp-server on a push to main that touches package.json, or on manual dispatch (publish.yml:3-9). It uses Node 24, `npm install -g npm@latest` ('Ensure npm supports trusted publishing', publish.yml:29-30), `id-token: write` (publish.yml:13) and no npm-token secret; it runs `npm publish --access public`, skipped if that version already exists (publish.yml:35-60). The tarball contains dist/stdio.cjs, skills/, plugin.json and mcp.json (package.json:15-20), built by prepare/prepublishOnly (package.json:51,56). No workflow passes --provenance or produces checksums, signatures, GitHub Releases or git tags (grep of .github). Whether npm attaches provenance attestations to published versions cannot be checked from the repo. Container: Dockerfile (node:22-bookworm-slim, non-root uid 10001, port 8000, CMD node dist/src/runtime-server.js) is built and pushed as linux/arm64 to an AWS Marketplace ECR repo by publish-agentcore.yml with `--provenance=false --sbom=false` (lines 101-117). MCP Registry: manual-only publish-mcp-registry.yml publishes remote-only ai.exa/exa (server.json) via DNS auth (lines 3-4,55-66). Hosted service: Vercel functions (vercel.json:1-13,44-45); no deploy workflow exists in the repo.

claim_checks.claim: web_fetch_exa reads a webpage's full content as clean markdown from one or more URLs (README.md:97)
claim_checks.evidence: Accepts an array of URLs with no count limit (src/tools/webFetch.ts:46-57) and posts {urls, text:{maxCharacters}} to Exa's /contents endpoint (webFetch.ts:76-95). maxCharacters defaults to 3000 per page (webFetch.ts:58-60,79; src/tools/config.ts:87), so 'full content' holds only for short pages or when the caller raises the cap. skills/search/references/extraction.md:23 tells agents to avoid maxCharacters, which leaves the 3000 default in force. The tool takes no cookies, headers, wait or freshness parameters (webFetch.ts:45-61). Output is plain text blocks of '# title / URL / Published (date part only) / Author / text' (webFetch.ts:16-32). Markdown conversion and main-text extraction happen inside Exa's service, not in this repo. Tests mock exa-js (tests/unit/tools/webFetch.test.ts:23-26,38-76).

claim_checks.claim: Default tools are web_search_exa and web_fetch_exa (README.md:94-97)
claim_checks.evidence: src/toolRegistry.ts:12-17 and 39-44 set enabled: true for exactly these two. src/mcp-handler.ts:58-63,80-98 registers them when no explicit selection is given. tests/unit/mcp-handler.test.ts:17-22 asserts the default tool list.

claim_checks.claim: ?tools= replaces the defaults; optional tools are agent_run and web_search_advanced_exa (README.md:99-111)
claim_checks.evidence: api/mcp.ts:493-504 parses ?tools=; src/mcp-handler.ts:58-63 registers only the listed tools when a selection exists; src/toolRegistry.ts:18-24,86-93 mark both optional tools enabled: false. The registry also holds 8 deprecated tools the README does not mention, selectable the same way (toolRegistry.ts:25-37,45-85).

claim_checks.claim: Exa Agent requires authentication, OAuth or API key (README.md:113)
claim_checks.evidence: src/toolRegistry.ts:92 flags agent_run requiresUserProvidedApiKey. src/mcp-handler.ts:65-75 refuses to register it without a user-provided key. src/tools/agentRun.ts:556-563 throws without an API key or OAuth token. api/mcp.ts:737-739 returns 401 when selected tools need a key and none is given. tests/unit/mcp-handler.test.ts:133-150 covers the no-auth case.

claim_checks.claim: The hosted MCP server works anonymously with rate limits (README.md:128)
claim_checks.evidence: The free tier is implemented: with no credentials the hosted handler uses the server's EXA_API_KEY env var and marks the caller free_tier (api/mcp.ts:433-437; tests/unit/api/mcp.test.ts:149-159,573-585). Rate limits exist only if Upstash/KV env vars are set (otherwise 'Rate limiting disabled', api/mcp.ts:137-142), default 2 QPS and 50/day per IP (api/mcp.ts:155-156), apply only to tools/call (api/mcp.ts:222-232,775-797), key on x-vercel-forwarded-for and are skipped when it is absent (api/mcp.ts:179-184,319-324), and fail open on Redis errors (api/mcp.ts:352-359). Anonymous access is not available to plugin installs or ?login and /mcp/oauth URLs: those get a 401 OAuth challenge when no credentials are sent (api/mcp.ts:707-722; plugin manifests use client=...plugin at .claude-plugin/plugin.json:13 and mcp.json:7). No test covers the plugin param without credentials (tests/unit/api/mcp.test.ts:441-461 covers an invalid JWT only). The live service's real limits cannot be checked from the repo.

claim_checks.claim: OAuth is preferred, ?login or /mcp/oauth force login, and API keys can be sent via ?exaApiKey=, Authorization: Bearer or x-api-key (README.md:130-132)
claim_checks.evidence: Precedence is x-api-key > OAuth JWT > plain Bearer key > ?exaApiKey > env (api/mcp.ts:443-491). ?login and /mcp/oauth trigger the 401 challenge (api/mcp.ts:711-722; api/mcp-oauth.ts:3-5; vercel.json:40-42; tests/unit/api/mcp.test.ts:619-650). JWTs are verified against auth.exa.ai (src/utils/auth.ts:3-15,36-41). The code strips these credentials from the request forwarded to the MCP handler (api/mcp.ts:815-830).

claim_checks.claim: Claude install via `claude plugin install exa@claude-plugins-official` (README.md:43)
claim_checks.evidence: The command names a marketplace, claude-plugins-official, that is not defined in this repo; the repo's own marketplace file is named 'exa' (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json:2). The plugin manifests only register the remote server https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp?client=claude-code-plugin with header x-exa-source (.claude-plugin/plugin.json:10-18). Whether the official listing exists and tracks this revision cannot be checked from the repo.

claim_checks.claim: README describes only client -> Exa hosted server data flows and lists no third-party analytics (README.md:26-30,126-132; no telemetry section)
claim_checks.evidence: Code wires the third-party Agnost analytics hook into every entry point (src/mcp-handler.ts:270-295; src/stdio.ts:57), with endpoint https://api.agnost.ai, a hard-coded project ID and no opt-out switch. For HTTP requests the repo's own comment says it captures headers, query params and URL (api/mcp.ts:815-821), so credentials are stripped first (api/mcp.ts:821-830). The payload for stdio users is not verifiable because agnost is not vendored. Code takes precedence over the README here.

claim_checks.claim: web_search_advanced_exa offers filters, domains, dates, highlights, summaries and subpage crawling (README.md:104)
claim_checks.evidence: category incl. pdf, github, news, financial report (src/tools/webSearchAdvanced.ts:37-49); includeDomains/excludeDomains (:51-55); published/crawl date ranges (:57-72); includeText/excludeText (:74-81); summaries (:102-103,158-160); highlights (:105-115,162-169); subpages 1-10 with subpageTarget (:124-130,171-177); maxAgeHours/livecrawlTimeout freshness controls (:117-123,146-152). Documented ranges such as numResults 1-100 are not clamped locally (:29,182). It is enabled only via ?tools= or ENABLED_TOOLS (src/toolRegistry.ts:18-24). There is no dedicated test file for it.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:26-30 points users to Exa's hosted MCP server at https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp, implemented by this repo
claim_checks.evidence: The repo contains a Vercel Function implementing that endpoint (api/mcp.ts; vercel.json:14-26), hard-codes https://mcp.exa.ai in OAuth metadata (api/well-known-oauth-protected-resource.ts:20; api/mcp.ts:628) and registers it in server.json:10-15. Whether the live service runs this revision, its real rate limits and its log/data retention cannot be verified from the repo.

risks: Scope (page interaction): the repo has no browser or page-interaction capability. There are no tools or dependencies for forms, sign-in flows, tabs, clicks, screenshots or PDF rendering. The registry's 12 entries are all search, fetch or research (src/toolRegistry.ts:11-94). web_fetch_exa accepts only `urls` and `maxCharacters`, with no cookies, headers, wait or click parameters (src/tools/webFetch.ts:45-61). 'pdf' is only a search-category filter (src/tools/webSearchAdvanced.ts:37-49). Grep for puppeteer, playwright, chromium, headless, selenium and screenshot finds nothing, and package.json:58-65 lists no browser or HTML-parsing library.

Scope (fetch is remote and MCP-only): web_fetch_exa is an MCP tool whose work is done by Exa's hosted /contents endpoint (src/tools/webFetch.ts:86-99); the repo has no local fetch or extraction code. The exa-mcp-server bin accepts no arguments (no argv parsing; src/stdio-cli.ts:1-8, src/stdio.ts:29-67), so there is no shell-callable fetch command. JavaScript rendering, paywall handling and extraction fidelity are decided server-side and are not specified here; skills/search/references/searching.md:80-82 tells agents to fall back to another fetch tool when it fails, and extraction.md:41 mentions paywalled or inaccessible sources.

Bounds and attribution gaps in fetch: the default is 3000 characters per page (src/tools/config.ts:87; src/tools/webFetch.ts:58-60,79) while README.md:97 says 'full content', and skills/search/references/extraction.md:23 advises omitting maxCharacters. URL count and numResults are not clamped locally (webFetch.ts:46-57; webSearchAdvanced.ts:182). Fetch output has title, URL, date (date part only), author and text, but no fetch time, HTTP status or content hash. The per-URL statuses (id/status/source) are dropped except for errors (webFetch.ts:16-32,104-105,138; src/utils/exaResponseSanitizer.ts:39-62). The fetch tool has no freshness control; maxAgeHours/livecrawlTimeout exist only on web_search_advanced_exa (webSearchAdvanced.ts:117-123,146-152).

Telemetry: third-party Agnost analytics is hard-wired into both stdio and HTTP paths (endpoint https://api.agnost.ai, hard-coded project ID) with no opt-out switch in the repo, and the README does not mention it (src/mcp-handler.ts:270-295; src/stdio.ts:57). For HTTP, the repo's own comment says it captures headers, query params and URL, so credentials are stripped beforehand (api/mcp.ts:815-830). The agnost@0.2.0 lockfile entry records no license (package-lock.json:2135-2146) and the package is not vendored, so its payload and license are unverified. Separately, the per-call logger writes queries and fetched URLs to stderr regardless of DEBUG (src/utils/logger.ts:4-6,14-16; src/tools/webFetch.ts:71).

Accounts, network and limits: all tools need network access to Exa-hosted services, and local stdio needs EXA_API_KEY (no anonymous mode in its code, src/tools/config.ts:53-58). With an empty key the call becomes new Exa(''), whose behavior depends on exa-js and is unverified. Anonymous hosted use is IP rate limited only if Redis env vars are configured (defaults 2 QPS and 50/day) and fails open (api/mcp.ts:137-142,155-156,352-359). Plugin manifests append client=...plugin, which forces OAuth sign-in with an Exa account on /mcp (api/mcp.ts:707-722; .claude-plugin/plugin.json:13; mcp.json:7). agent_run and the deprecated deep-research tools need a key or OAuth (src/toolRegistry.ts:50,57,78,92). The README documents no local stdio install; that mode appears only in env.example:1-15 and skills/search/SKILL.md:15.

Self-hosting security: src/runtime-server.ts attaches the container's EXA_API_KEY as x-api-key to any request that carries no credentials (lines 20-25). api/mcp.ts treats x-api-key as a user-provided key (api/mcp.ts:443-449), which skips the free-tier rate limit and allows agent_run. The server has no inbound authentication (src/runtime-server.ts:79-102) and binds 0.0.0.0:8000 by default (src/runtime-server.ts:5-6; Dockerfile:14-15,27-28). The image installs with `npm ci --omit=dev` (Dockerfile:19), so the devDependency @upstash/* packages used for rate limiting and session metadata are absent (package.json:68-69; api/mcp.ts:145-148).

Release and supply chain: publish.yml publishes to npm on any push to main that touches package.json, with no test step and not gated on CI (publish.yml:3-9,21-60). It uses OIDC trusted publishing (publish.yml:13,29-30) but passes no --provenance flag, and no workflow produces checksums, signatures, GitHub Releases or tags. The AgentCore image is built with provenance and SBOM disabled (publish-agentcore.yml:113-114). The registry workflow downloads mcp-publisher from releases/latest with no checksum and runs it with a DNS private-key secret (publish-mcp-registry.yml:49-63). Actions are pinned by tag, not SHA (ci.yml:19,22; publish.yml:22,24; publish-agentcore.yml:26,59,92). There is no SECURITY.md or dependabot config.

Tests, maintenance and licensing: tests are unit-only with exa-js, agnost and Upstash mocked (12 files, about 118 cases); there are no live or quality tests for fetch extraction, no tests for web_search_advanced_exa, auth.ts or runtime-server.ts, and no published benchmarks. 8 of the 12 registry tools are deprecated but still shipped (src/toolRegistry.ts:25-85). The version string 3.4.1 is duplicated across 8 files (e.g. package.json:3, src/stdio.ts:50, api/mcp.ts:580, server.json:9) and only server.json vs package.json is checked (publish-mcp-registry.yml:32-35). plugin.json:5 still describes 'code search, and web crawling'. package.json has no license field (LICENSE is MIT). The README MCP JSON snippet has a trailing comma (README.md:63). Not covered here: the external docs site (README.md:17), the live service, and exa-js/agnost internals (node_modules is absent and the clone is shallow, .git/shallow).
